question: Will the FAO Vegetable Oil Price Index for September 2026 exceed its August 2026 value of 196.9?

calls.reasoning: Reference class (FAO veg oil index m/m changes, 1990-2026) rises in ~53% of months; conditional on three consecutive prior increases, continuation runs ~60-65%. ~68% of the September averaging window is already observed. Component build-up for Sept-to-date vs August averages: palm +1.5 to +2% (CPO FOB Malaysia Aug ~$1,130 -> Sep ~$1,147; RBD olein nearby $1,172 -> $1,192; Indonesian CPO $1,222 -> $1,245), CBOT soyoil Dec +3% ($1,500 on 12 Aug -> $1,550 on 16 Sep), sunflower -4 to -8% (Russia FOB $1,310-1,320 -> $1,250-1,260; India CIF $1,487 -> $1,430), rapeseed -1 to -2%. At FAO's palm-heavy 2014-16 export-share weights this nets to roughly +0.3 to +0.6%, i.e. ~197.5-198.1. Threshold asymmetry helps: August precise was 196.86, so a rise of only ~0.05% publishes as 197.0 and clears 196.9. Main downside paths are a bigger sunflower collapse on the record 62 Mt crop, a soyoil give-back on weakening US biofuel demand expectations, and a late-September palm slide on 3 Mt Malaysian stocks plus first-half September exports down 18-26% m/m. No market prices this contract.
calls.dossier:
RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: Resolves off the FAO Vegetable Oil Price Index (nominal) for September 2026 as FIRST PUBLISHED in the 2 October 2026 FAO Food Price Index release — not off BMD palm futures, not off any revised August figure, not off the headline FFPI composite. FAO publishes the sub-index to one decimal; August 2026 printed 196.9 (precise 196.86, per FAO's August release). Threshold is fixed at 196.9 and a September print of exactly 196.9 resolves NO. FAO's confirmed 2026 release calendar lists 2 October as the September date (prior dates 7 Aug, 4 Sep all met). Annulment only if no September figure by 31 Oct 2026.

EVENT WINDOW: the index is the average of component quotations over the calendar month 1–30 September 2026 per the criteria; as of 2026-09-21T06:50Z, ~20.3 of 30 days (~68%) elapsed. Publication follows the window's close by two days.

INDEX CONSTRUCTION: four components — palm, soy, rapeseed, sunflower oil — weighted by average export trade shares 2014–2016 (base 2014–2016 = 100). Implied export-value shares for that period put palm at roughly 0.45–0.60, soy ~0.16–0.24, sunflower ~0.16–0.20, rapeseed ~0.07–0.13; FAO does not publish the exact vector, so the weighting is itself a source of spread.

STATUS QUO: the index has risen three consecutive months (Jun→Jul→Aug), reaching its highest level since June 2022; the July→August step was +1.1 points (+0.6%).

calls.reference_class: Month-over-month changes in the FAO Vegetable Oil Price Index, 1990-2026, and specifically months following three consecutive monthly increases

calls.reasoning: Palm oil (~45-50% of the FAO veg-oil sub-index) rose through August ($1,145 -> $1,195 RBD olein FOB prompt) and has HELD that end-August level all of September ($1,190-1,195; Indonesian CPO Oct $1,250, near a 21-month high). A month that ended above its own average, followed by a flat month, mechanically delivers a higher monthly average — this carry-over is the core of the call. WTI averaged ~$80 in August vs ~$96-104 in September (Hormuz strikes), supporting biofuel feedstock demand; CBOT soyoil is flat-to-up (Aug range 66.3-71.3, Sep 68.0-70.3) after a 7.2% Sep 2 jump on EPA SRE reallocation. Offsets: sunflower under record-crop harvest pressure (Ukrainian seed $485 -> $445-465 during September) and rapeseed steady-to-soft — but both fell in August too and the index still rose 0.6%. Weighting palm +2%, soy +1%, sun -3%, rape 0% gives roughly +0.5 to +1.0% m/m (~197.9-198.9). NO needs a sharp final-week reversal (crude de-escalation) or sunflower collapsing harder than seed data implies; bearish palm fundamentals (Malaysian Sep 1-15 exports -17.8 to -25.6% m/m, rising stocks) are real but not yet in quotes. ~67% of the pricing month is already observed and is running above August.

Unconditional up-month frequency for the FAO veg oil index is ~52-55%; conditional on three consecutive rises and an upward within-August price path, ~60-65%. Partial-month data (Sept 1-21, ~2/3 of the observation window) points the same way: nearby Bursa CPO averaged ~4,674 MYR in September vs ~4,590 in August (+1.8%, ringgit near flat vs USD); Chicago soyoil ~$1,550-1,600/t vs ~$1,500 on 12 Aug; European rapeseed oil ~$1,435-1,460 FOB NL vs ~$1,390-1,420, with Euronext rapeseed +4.6% MoM; Brent up ~22% on the month to $109 supports biodiesel-linked demand. The offset is sunflower oil, falling hard on a record 63.65 Mt crop (India CIF $1,485->$1,430; Ukrainian offers toward $1,100-1,120). Export-share-weighted, components net to roughly +0.5 to +0.9%, i.e. ~197.9-198.6, but component and weight error plus 7 remaining trading days give ~1.2pp SD, and the past week showed broad softening (palm off its 21-month high, record Malaysian stocks, Sept 1-15 exports -17.8/-25.6%). Small extra NO mass for an exact 196.9 tie.

calls.reference_class: Month-over-month changes in the FAO Vegetable Oil Price Index (1990-2026), and the subset of months following three consecutive monthly increases

calls.reasoning: Threshold is effectively 'any month-on-month rise': August printed 196.9 off a precise 196.86, so only +0.046% is needed to publish 197.0. ~68% of the September averaging window is already observed and running above August. The decisive fact no run retrieved: FAO prices this index off European quotations (palm crude CIF NW Europe, sun oil EU FOB NW Europe port, rape and soy oil Dutch FOB ex-mill, weights from 2014-16 export values) - so the -16% Ukrainian Danube sunoil collapse is the wrong instrument (Fastmarkets: Black Sea down ~7% m/m), rapeseed on FAO's Dutch basis is UP (~$1,415-25 Aug to $1,435-60 Sep, Euronext seed +4.6%) not down, and palm's CIF-Europe quote is freight-inflated by the Hormuz/Red Sea crude spike. Re-weighted, components net to roughly +0.8 to +1.0% (~198.5). NO needs the last ~6-7 quotation days to run 2.5-4% below current levels, or EU new-crop sunoil (9.73 Mt EU harvest peaking in September) to fall far harder than Black Sea data implies, plus ~2% for an exact 196.9 tie.
calls.reconciliation: DISPUTES: (1) which price basis FAO uses per component; (2) size of the sunflower drag (-3% vs -8% vs -16%); (3) rapeseed direction; (4) existence of a market; (5) how much the unobserved final ~9 days can undo; (6) dispersion. CHECKS RUN (5 max): FAO Oilcrops Price Indices page FETCHED - confirms ten European quotations (palm crude cif NW Eur; sun oil EU fob NW Eur port; rape oil Dutch fob ex-mill; soybean oil Dutch fob ex-mill; palm kernel/coconut cif Rotterdam; minors) weighted by 2014-16 export values. This settles (1) and reframes (2) and (3): the Danube/India-CIF sunoil series Runs 1 and 3 leaned on are not FAO's instrument, and Fastmarkets independently reports Black Sea sunoil down 'at least 7%' over a month, so the drag is nearer Run 2's read; Run 3's FOB Netherlands rapeseed series IS FAO's basis and shows September ABOVE August, so Runs 1 and 2 had the rapeseed sign wrong; and palm on a CIF-Europe basis carries the September freight/crude spike, so it likely rose more than the FOB Malaysia +1.5-2%. Market search: no Polymarket, Manifold or bookmaker contract on the sub-index; Kalshi's KXFAOFPI series prices the HEADLINE five-group FFPI, a different instrument (veg oils ~1/5 weight, different threshold, different fine print), so it is evidence at best and I did not anchor on it - no usable price retrieved. EMPTY CHECKS: no nowcast, partial, or third-party estimate of the September sub-index exists; FAO publishes no exact weight vector, so component weights remain estimated from 2014-16 export values and stay a genuine source of spread. Late-window check: palm rangebound on 21 Sep (Dec 4,896-4,913 MYR), off its 21-month high but still above August levels. JUDGMENT, unresolved by evidence: how much of the record-supply/weak-export bearishness lands inside September's remaining quotation days versus October - I take the reading that it mostly lands in October, since physical CIF Europe quotes have held $1,190-1,250 all month. Net: three of the bearish inputs the lower runs used were basis errors, so I sit above Runs 1 and 3; the EU new-crop sunoil channel that the correct basis exposes keeps me just under Run 2.

disagreements.verdict: FALSE - FAO's Oilcrops page lists palm crude CIF NW Europe and sun oil EU FOB NW Europe port, plus Dutch fob ex-mill for soy and rape; weights from 2014-16 export values. All three runs proxied with origin-basis series.

disagreements.claim: Sunflower drags the index down 4-8% (or more) in September
disagreements.verdict: Overstated on FAO's basis. The -16% figure is the discounted Danube route; Fastmarkets puts Black Sea sunoil at ~-7% m/m and EU FOB NW Europe moves less. Residual risk noted: the EU's own 9.73 Mt new crop harvests in September, which is exactly this quote's exposure.

disagreements.claim: Rapeseed oil quotations fell in September
disagreements.verdict: FALSE on FAO's basis - FOB Netherlands rose from ~$1,415-1,425 to $1,435-1,460, Euronext rapeseed +4.55% m/m. Runs 1 and 2 had the sign inverted.

disagreements.claim: A prediction market prices this event
disagreements.verdict: No. Nothing on Polymarket, Manifold, or bookmakers; Kalshi's KXFAOFPI covers the headline composite only, a different resolution instrument. Not used as an anchor.

disagreements.claim: The final ~9 unobserved days can plausibly reverse the month
disagreements.verdict: Not broken by evidence. Arithmetically the remaining ~32% of the window must average ~2.5-4% below current levels to null a +0.8-1.0% build-up. I price that, plus the EU sunoil tail and a ~2% exact-196.9 tie, at ~21% total.

disagreements.claim: Dispersion on the component build-up is ~1.2pp SD
disagreements.verdict: Carried forward from Run 3 - reasonable, since unpublished weights and my use of proxy series for European quotes offset the variance already retired by two-thirds of the window closing.

calls.reference_class: Month-on-month changes in the FAO Vegetable Oil Price Index (1990-2026), conditioned on three consecutive prior increases and on two-thirds of the new month's quotations already averaging above the prior month
